newsitem.title: UK: UK mercenary now in embassy in Papua New Guinea.
newsitem.headline: UK mercenary now in embassy in Papua New Guinea.

text.p: A British commander hired to crush a revolt in Papua New Guinea has been released into the care of British diplomats, the Foreign Office said on Saturday.
A spokesman in London said retired colonel Tim Spicer, the chief executive of London-based Sandline International, would appear in court on Monday.
"We have had confirmation from our High Commissioner in Papua New Guinea that Tim Spicer has been handed over and is now in his care," he told Reuters.
"He has been charged with possessing a firearm and 40 rounds of ammunition and has been bailed to appear in court on Monday morning," he added.

Spicer, a former top U.N. peacekeeper in Bosnia who served in the Falklands and Gulf wars, is chief executive of Sandline International, which signed a $36 million dollar contract with Papua New Guinea in January to provide commandos and hardware to crush a nine-year guerrilla uprising on copper-rich Bougainville island.

The worst crisis in the 22 years since Papua New Guinea won independence from Australia began on Monday when army commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok suddenly turned on Sir Julius Chan, demanding that he quit and terminate the mercenary contract.
